“The Tale of Benjamin Bunny” is a part of a collection of stories entitled “The Complete Adventures of Peter Rabbit”.  This collection is a public domain book about a curious little rabbit who wants to go exploring.  In this tale, Peter is nervous about Mr. McGregor coming back.  He is also afraid to go home to his mother without his clothes.  His cousin, Benjamin Bunny, helps him find his way back home safely.  

This story is read aloud and includes sound effects from iMovie and YouTube using free usage sounds.  

We hope you enjoy and join us every week for a new story!

McGregor in her best bonnet as soon as they had passed a little Benjamin bunny slid down into the road and set off with a hop skip and a jump to call upon his relations who lived in the wood at the back of mr. McGregor's garden that wood was full of rabbit holes and in the neatest sandiest hole of all lived Benjamin's aunt and his cousin's Flopsy Mopsy Cottontail and Peter old mrs. rabbit was a widow she earned her living by knitting rabbit wool mittens and Muffet ease I once bought a parrot of bazaar she also sold herbs and rosemary tea and rabbit tobacco which is what we call lavender little Benjamin did not very much want to see his aunt he came round the back of the fir tree and nearly tumbled upon the top of his cousin Peter Peter was sitting by herself he looked poorly and was dressed in a red cotton pocket-handkerchief Peter said little Benjamin and a Whisperer who has got her clothes Peter replied the Scarecrow and mr. McGregor's garden and described how he had been chased about the garden and had dropped his shoes and coat little Benjamin sat down beside his cousin and assured him that mr. McGregor had gone out in a gate and mrs. McGregor's garden Peter's coat and shoes were plainly to be seen upon the Scarecrow topped with an old Tam O'Shanter of mr. McGregor's [Music] little Benjamin said it spoils people's clothes to squeeze under the gate the proper way to get in is to climb down a pear tree Peter fell down headfirst but it was of no consequence as the bed below was newly raped and quite soft it had been sewn with lettuces they left a great many odd little foot marks all over the bed especially little Benjamin who was wearing claws little Benjamin said that the first thing to be done was to get back Peters clothes in order that they may be able to use the pocket handkerchief they took them off the Scarecrow there had been much rain during the night there was water in the shoes and the coat was somewhat shrunk Benjamin tried on the Tam O'Shanter but it was too big for him [Music] then he suggested that they should fill the pocket-handkerchief with onions as a little present for his aunt Peter did not seem to be enjoying himself he kept hearing noises Benjamin on the contrary was perfectly at home and ate a lettuce leaf he felt like he was in the habit running into the garden with his father to get lettuces for their Sunday dinner the name of Benjamin's Papa was old mr. Benjamin bunny the lettuces certainly were very fine Peter did not eat anything he said he should like to go home presently they dropped half the onions little Benjamin said it was not possible to get back up to P retreat with a load of vegetables he led the weight boldly towards the other under the garden they went along a little walk on planks under a cyanide brick wall my sat on their doorsteps cracking cherry stones they wait at Peter Rabbit and little Benjamin bunny presently Peter let the pocket-handkerchief go again they got amongst flowerpots and frames and tubs Peter heard noises worse than ever his eyes were as big as lollipops he was a step or two in the front of his cousin when he suddenly stopped this is what those little rabbits saw around that corner little Benjamin took one look and then in half a minute or less in no time he hid himself in Peter and the onions underneath a large basket a cat got up and stretched herself and came and sneaked at the basket perhaps she liked the smell of onions anyway she went down on top of the box where she sat there for five hours I cannot draw you a picture of Peter Benjamin underneath the basket because it was quite dark and because the smell of onions was fearful it made you rabbit and little Benjamin cry the Sun got ran behind the wood and it was quite late in the afternoon but still the cat sent upon that basket at length there was a pitter-patter pitter-patter and some bits of mortar fell from the wall above the cat looked up and saw old mr. Benjamin bunny prancing along the top of the wall of the upper terrace he was smoking a pipe of rabbit tobacco and had a little switch in his hand he was looking for his son old mr. bunny had no opinion whatever of cats he took a tremendous jump off the top of the wall onto the top of the cat and cuffed it off the basket and kicked it into the greenhouse scratching off a handful of fur the cat was too much surprised to scratch back when old mr. funny had driven the cat into the greenhouse he locked the door then he came back to the basket and took out his son Benjamin by the ears and whipped him with a little switch and he took out his nephew Peter then he took out the handkerchief of onions and marched out of the garden when mr. McGregor returned about half an hour later he observed several things which perplexed him it looked as though some person had been walking all over the garden and a pair of clogs only the foot marks were too ridiculously little also he could not understand how the cat could have managed to shut herself up inside the greenhouse locking the door upon the outside when Peter got home his mother forgave him because she was so glad to see that he had found his shoes and coat Cottontail and Peter folded up the pocket handkerchief and old mrs. rabbit strung up the onions and hung them from the kitchen ceiling with the bunches of herbs and the rabbit tobacco the end [Applause] [Music]

McGregor's garden your father had an accident there he was put in a pie by mrs. McGregor [Music] now run along and don't get into any mischief I'm going out [Music] then old mrs. rabbit took a basket and her umbrella and went through the woods to the bakers she brought a loaf of brown bread and five currant buns [Music] Flopsy Mopsy and Cottontail who are good little bunnies went down the lane to gather blackberries [Music] but Peter who is very naughty ran straight away to mr. McGregor's garden and squeezed under the gate first he ate some lettuces and some French beef and then he ate some radishes and then feeling rather sick he went to look for some parsley [Music] wait a minute but round the end of the cucumber frame whom should he meet but mr. McGregor mr. McGregor was on his hands and knees planting out young cabbages but he jumped up and ran after Peter waving a rake and yelling out stop thief [Music] Peter was most dreadfully frightened he rushed all over the garden for he had forgotten the way back to the gate he lost one of his shoes among the cabbages and the other shoe amongst the potatoes [Music] after losing them he ran on four legs and went faster so that I think he might have gotten away altogether if he had not unfortunately run into a gooseberry net and got caught by the large buttons on his jacket it was a blue jacket with brass buttons quite new Peter gave himself up for lost and shed big tears but his sobs were overheard by some friendly sparrows he flew to him great excitement and implored him to assert himself mr. McGregor came up with a sieve which he intended to pop up on the top of Peter but Peter wriggled out just in time leaving his jacket behind him [Music] and rushed into the toolshed and jumped into it it would have been a beautiful thing to hide in if it had not had so much water in it mr. McGregor was after him in no time and tried to put his foot upon Peter who jumped out of a window upsetting three plants the window was too small for mr. McGregor and he was tired of running after Peter he went back to his work [Music] Peter sat down to rest he was out of breath now I'm trembling with fright and he had not had the least idea of which way to go also he was very damp was sitting in that camp after some time he began to wander about going Liberty Liberty not very fast at all and looking around he found a door in a wall but it was locked and there was no room for a fat little rabbit to squeeze underneath an old mouse was running in and out over the stone doorstep carrying peas and bees to her family in the wood Peter asked her the way to the gate but she had such a large pea in her mouth that she could not answer she only shook her head at him Peter began to cry then he tried to find his way straight across the garden but he became more and more puzzled presently he came to a pond where mr. mcgregor filled his water cans a white cat was staring at some goldfish she sat very still but now and then the tip of her tail twitched as if it were alive Peter thought it was best to go away without speaking to her he had heard about cats from his cousin little Benjamin bunny [Music] he went back towards the toolshed but suddenly quite close to him he heard the noise of a hope scratch scratch scratch scritch Peter scuttered underneath the bushes but presently as nothing happened he came out and climbed upon a wheelbarrow and peeped over the first thing that he saw was mr. McGregor hoeing some onions his back was turned towards Peter and beyond him was the gate Peter got down very quietly off the wheelbarrow and started running as fast as he could go along straight walk behind some blackcurrant bushes mr. McGregor caught sight of him at the corner Peter did not care he slipped underneath the gate and was safe at last in the wood outside the garden mr. McGregor hung up the little jacket and the shoes for a scarecrow to frighten the Blackbirds [Music] Peter never stopped running or looked behind him until he got home to the big fir-tree he was so tired that he flopped down upon the nice soft sand on the floor of the rabbit-hole and shut his eyes his mother was busy cooking she wondered what he had done with his clothes it was the second little jacket in pair of shoes that Peter had lost in a fortnight I am sorry to say that Peter was not very well during the evening his mother put him in bed and mades him some chamomile tea and she gave a dose of it to Peter one tablespoonful to be taken at bedtime but Flopsy Mopsy and Cottontail had bread and milk and blackberries for supper the end [Music]

going straight into a blood vessel now we were in the blood but it did not look red blood is not just a red liquid explained Miss Frizzle blood is made of cells floating in a clear liquid those cells look like Red Rubber saucers someone called out those are red blood cells Miss Frizzle said red blood cells carry oxygen from the lungs to all the cells of the body here and there a white blood cell the two Chambers on the right side of the heart took en used blood from the body and pumped it to the lungs in the lungs the red cells picked up fresh oxygen from the lungs our red blood cells carried us back to the heart this time we were on the left side of the heart the side that pumps fresh blood back to the body again kids it looks as if these red blood cells are on their way to the brain said Miss Frizzle when we reach the brain we let go of our red blood cells and squeezed out of the blood vessel it was hard to believe that this wrinkled gray blob was the control center of the body Miss climbing down the bones of the spine inside the bones was a spinal cord a thick bundle of nerve cells stretching from the brain smaller bundles of nerve cells branched out from each side of the spinal cord these carried nerve messages to all parts of the body we followed some nerves that went to the leg muscles the leg muscles were working hard they needed a lot of energy they used up a lot of food and oxygen from our blood the heart was beating faster to carry fresh blood to the muscle cells we entered a nearby blood vessel the blood was moving so fast we were afraid we were going to lose each other but at that moment the school bus floated by what a relief we jumped on and went up through the heart in the lungs again just the way we went before when we emerged from the bloodstream we were in a huge open space where are we asked a kid Miss Frizzle explained children this is the nasal cavity the what we asked the inside of the nose said the fr is suddenly we heard a deafening noise it sounded like ah ah uh then we heard CH a tremendous blast of air hit the Bus full force we flew forward spinning around and around and around we were going so fast we couldn't see anything but we could tell we were getting bigger and then thud we landed there we were back at school and there was Arnold in the school parking lot blowing his nose Arnold we said the trip was amazing you should have been there back in the classroom it was business as usual Miss Frizzle made us draw a chart of the human body for the bulletin board at last everything was quiet in Miss frizzle's class everything of course except her dress the end

the corner and read [Music] when he gave a book report he spoke Softly at lunch Stanley quietly ate his sandwich with mayonnaise even though he'd said no toppings please when Stanley's classmates played Sports he sat on the bench and tapped his feet Stanley dreamed of tap dancing on a big stage but he was afraid to tell anyone except his pet mice squeaker and nibbles after school Stanley sometimes helped the janitor when no one was nearby he switched his shoes weather in an empty classroom dark library or quiet gym Stanley tap danced to his heart's content but if anyone came around Reynolds replied Talent should be shared Stanley had only weeks to overcome his shyness he ripped for his rodents flapped for feral cats and ball changed for birds still his stage fright stayed with the talent show quickly approaching Stanley mustered the courage to dance for a classmate [Music] what do you think he asked Tom cheered you're really good he felt a glimmer of hope after school Stanley slipped into the auditorium to practice stage lights glared he closed his eyes and danced Stanley finished with a series of spinning taps Applause swelled who Stanley's mouth fell open the house lights came up it looks like you're in the right place at least said the Drama teacher you just walked into auditions at the talent show Stanley watched from the wings as the student played the saxophone a unicyclist cycled and a singer inspired the audience to sing along as he watched Stanley shrank smaller and smaller how can I compete with such talent at last Stanley's turn came he skittered onto the stage Shuffle heal flap stomp riff with each move he gained confidence Pride even Joy I've practiced these steps a thousand times Stanley completed his number and took a bow the crowd Rose I did it he tapped off the stage as if dancing on air when principal Reynolds handed out the talent show prizes Stanley won first place you were right Stanley admitted Talent should be shared and though Stanley performed whenever asked and spoke up more and more he still didn't like parties or Sports but his favorite audience remained Quaker and nibbles the end [Applause]

announced we were going on a class trip to the Science Museum we were going to see an exhibit about how our bodies get energy from the food we eat the trip started out like any other trip we rad to the museum in the old school bus along the way we stopped at a park for lunch when it was time to go everyone got back on the bus everyone but Arnold he was still at the picnic table daydreaming and she said the small intestine was a coiled up Hollow tube the inner walls of the tube were covered with tiny fingers called Villi in the Villi are tiny blood vessels food molecules are taken into these blood vessels said Miss Frizzle once the food is in the blood it can travel all over the body we felt ourselves getting even smaller and Miss Frizzle started driving into one of the Villi she was going straight into a blood vessel now we were in the blood but it did not look red blood is not just a red liquid explained Miss Frizzle blood is made of cells floating in a clear liquid those cells look like Red Rubber saucers someone called out those are red blood cells Miss Frizzle said red blood cells carry oxygen from the lungs to all the cells of the body here and there a white blood cell the two Chambers on the right side of the heart took en used blood from the body and pumped it to the lungs in the lungs the red cells picked up fresh oxygen from the lungs our red blood cells carried us back to the heart this time we were on the left side of the heart the side that pumps fresh blood back to the body again kids it looks as if these red blood cells are on their way to the brain said Miss Frizzle when we reach the brain we let go of our red blood cells and squeezed out of the blood vessel it was hard to believe that this wrinkled gray blob was the control center of the body Miss Frizzle said the brain is made up of billions of busy Nerf cells they are constantly sending and receiving messages from the eyes ears muscles and other parts of the body too we left the head by climbing down the bones of the spine inside the bones was a spinal cord a thick bundle of nerve cells stretching from the brain smaller bundles of nerve cells branched out from each side of the spinal cord these carried nerve messages to all parts of the body we followed some nerves that went to the leg muscles the leg muscles were working hard they needed a lot of energy they used up a lot of food and oxygen from our blood the heart was beating faster to carry fresh blood to the muscle cells we entered a nearby blood vessel the blood was moving so fast we were afraid we were going to lose each other but at that moment the school bus floated by what a relief we jumped on and went up through the heart in the lungs again just the way we went before when we emerged from the bloodstream we were in a huge open space where are we asked a kid Miss Frizzle explained children this is the nasal cavity the what we asked the inside of the nose said the fr is suddenly we heard a deafening noise it cleaned_subtitles: Kind: captions Language: en Hello, story timers. Have you ever felt like things were just too bright, too loud, or just too much? I know I have, and our friend in this story has, too. Join along with us and listen to Too Much. Too Much, an overwhelming day, written by Jolene Kitier. Illustrated by Angel Chang. Alarm clock beeps. I quiver quake. The noise is loud and my ears ache. The sun is shining. Time to rise. The light is bright and hurts my eyes. Scrubbing, rubbing, washcloths rough. The water is cold. Please stop. enough. When I eat, I don't like crunch. Soft bananas. I'll munch a bunch. No, not that shirt. I want to shout. Sharp, itchy tag. Please cut it out. It's cold outside. I think you grew. This coat's too tight. What can I do? Playground friends crowd in touch. Someone hugs me. That's too much. Too loud. Too bright. Too itchy. Too tight. Overwhelmed. I don't want to play. Sheet. Hug, please, is what I say. A gentle hug and I feel brave. That careful squeeze is what I crave. When I can, I'll try to say just what I need to change my day. Quiet time, dark place, soft shirt, personal space. Not loud, not bright, not itchy, not tight. I take deep breaths. You hold my hand. I'm so thankful that you understand. With time and space, I know I'll find a peaceful place to still my mind. When feelings go on overload, I pause and breathe and all is slowed. The end. Thanks for listening. In the heart of Whimsywood, where mushrooms whispered secrets and stars twinkled down at tea parties, there lived a little skeleton named Skelly Nibble Bones. Oh, what if no one wants to be friends with me? The flowers seemed to shy away when he tiptoed by, and the bunnies always bounced off before he could say hello. [Music] So, Skellyy spent his days skipping stones over the moon pond and talking to his pet worm, Sir Wrigleton. "They think I'm too spooky," he sighed. [Music] But Skellyy wasn't spooky at all. He liked hopscotch and honey cakes. He whistled tunes on his wishbone flute and painted smiley faces on pebbles. One sundappled afternoon, Skellyy heard a curious sound. Tick, tink, tap. It was coming from behind the old jelly bean bush. Peeking past the candy colored leaves, Skellyy saw someone small, strange, and shimmering. A tiny robot with copper cheeks. "Oh," gasped Skellyy. "I didn't know anyone else came here." The robot blinked. You're not scared of me. Only if you're not scared of me, Skellyy said with a big grin. The robot's gears clicked softly. I'm Tinka Talk. I make wind up music boxes, but everyone says I'm too clanky. Skellyy sat beside her. I clank too, he whispered. Let's clank together. [Music] So they did. They built castles of sugar cubes, danced to Tinka's musical gears, and made hats out of dandelions and buttonweed. Skellyy laughed until his bones rattled like tambourines. Tinka smiled so wide. In the middle of a twinkling forest lived a cheerful skeleton named Skellyy. He loved nighttime walks under a silvery moon. He also loved soft music and his very best friends, three friendly witches. Bone berry pie. But I've never made it before. The witches blinked. Boneber berries. Why, yes, they grow in the whispering woods, said Skellyy proudly. I'll pick them tonight. The witches looked worried. "Be careful. The woods can be very tricky after dark," said Tanzy. But Skellyy was already bouncing down the path, humming his bone rattling tune. "La clink, la clink." [Music] In the woods, strange things rustled. Owls blinked, shadows danced. Skellyy tiptoed, searching high and low. Where are you little bone berries? Suddenly, pop. A bush puffed pink smoke in his face. A chew. Skellyy sneezed, spinning in circles. When the smoke cleared, he realized something. Oh, I'm lost. Back at the cottage, Willow stared at her tea. Skelly's been gone way too long. Tany declared right away, "I'll get my moon map." The three witches called on their friend Greta to help and they all flew off on their broomsticks, their scarves trailing stardust. Skellyy, Skellyy, they all called out. In the woods, Skellyy sat on a mossy rock, sighing. I just wanted to bring something special. Then Hazel landed right beside him. "We were so worried," said Tansy, wrapping him in a warm scarf.
